title: Incident Closure and Customer Reconciliation Procedure
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This page defines the canonical closure workflow for incidents that impact customer-facing LLM inference (hosted API, Dedicated, Private). It focuses on the handoffs, artifact collection, stakeholder notifications, and the customer reconciliation (credits/credits-decision) process required to fully close an incident. This is the single source of truth used by responders, SRE, Legal, and Customer Success for incident finalization.

Goals
- Ensure consistent, auditable closure for incidents that meet our SLA or customer-impact thresholds.
- Deliver clear, timely, and brand-safe customer communications.
- Ensure correct calculation and approval of any usage credits or reimbursement.
- Create actionable postmortems and closure artifacts that drive follow-up work.

When to use this doc
- Severity 1 and 2 incidents that impact production API latency, availability, or model correctness for customers.
- Any incident where SLO deviation was >5% or any customer-visible outage longer than 15 minutes.

Key roles and responsibilities
- Incident Commander (IC): owns incident timeline, final narrative, and closure decision.
- Bridge Operator: runs the communications bridge and evidence collection.
- SRE Lead: validates metrics, SLO breach magnitude, and technical remediation steps.
- CS (Customer Success) Liaison: coordinates customer notices and credit reconciliation.
- Legal/Compliance: reviews language for regulated customers and approves settlement language.
- Engineering Product Owner: triages follow-up bugs and prioritizes mitigations.

One-line closure criteria (healthy pipeline)
1) Service functional and passing primary SLOs for 2 full 15-minute windows;
2) Root cause identified or a documented mitigation/rollback that prevents recurrence;
3) Customer communications issued (initial ack, 1+ updates as appropriate, final summary);
4) Credits decision recorded and approved when required;
5) Postmortem draft created and assigned for review.

Incident closure checklist (actionable steps)
1. Immediate stabilization confirmed
   - Confirm API endpoints responding and error rates returned to baseline.
   - Verify key model-serving metrics: token throughput, kv cache hit-rate, GPU saturation, queue depth.

2. Evidence capture (bridge operator)
   - Attach: timeline.log, top-5 error traces, representative request/response pairs, Grafana snapshot URLs.
   - Export SLO detector evidence: query used, raw-timeseries CSV, alert triggers.

3. Customer communications (CS + IC)
   - Send initial acknowledgement within 30 minutes of Pager trigger (if incident is customer-impacting).
   - Send regular updates every 60 minutes or on milestone (stabilized, mitigation, rollback).
   - Publish final incident summary within 24 hours.

4. SLO impact & credit determination (SRE Lead + CS)
   - Calculate impact window: start/end times when service was below SLO.
   - Calculate affected customer population: tenant list or all-hosted API customers during window.
   - Refer to SLA credit policy table (below) and propose credit amount.
   - Obtain CS + Finance sign-off for credit issuance.

5. Postmortem authoring (IC and Eng PO)
   - Create a postmortem page using the standard template and link incident artifacts.
   - Assign action items (owner + due date) and set remediation priority.

6. Formal closure and archive
   - IC closes incident after confirming all above items are completed.
   - Move artifacts to the incident evidence archive (GCS bucket path in evidence attachment).
   - Notify execs and update status page (if public-facing).

SLA credit policy (summary table)
| SLA deviation | Typical credit (hosted API customers) | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| < 5% deviation or < 15 minutes | No credit | Handled via operational apology only |
| 5% - 15% deviation or 15-60 minutes | 5% service credit for impacted billing cycle | Requires CS approval |
| 15% - 50% deviation or 60-180 minutes | 10% - 25% service credit, tiered by customer impact | Finance & Legal review recommended |
| > 50% deviation or > 180 minutes | Case-by-case; potential pro-rated refunds | Exec + Legal approval required |

Credit calculation worked example
- Incident window: 2025-02-14T02:13Z to 2025-02-14T03:02Z (49 minutes)
- Affected tenants: 1200 hosted tokens/day plan, 300 enterprise customers with active calls in window
- Measured SLO deviation: 23% above error budget baseline
- Proposed credit: 15% credit for impacted billing period for enterprise tenants; 5% one-time credit for small-hosted tenants

Customer communications templates
- Use the templates below verbatim where applicable. Replace tokens in {{double_curly}} with values. Keep CS and Legal in the loop when language crosses regulated accounts.

Template: Initial acknowledgement (30-minute template)
Subject: We’re investigating an issue affecting Redwood Inference API
Hello {{customer_name}},
We detected an incident affecting some Redwood Inference API requests beginning at {{start_time}} UTC. Our on-call team is actively investigating. We will follow up within 30 minutes with an update or sooner if we have new information.
Impact: {{brief-impact}}
What we’re doing: stabilizing affected services, collecting evidence, and routing traffic to fallbacks where possible.
If you need immediate support, reply to this message and we will escalate.
Sincerely,
Redwood Inference Support

Template: Status update (periodic)
Subject: Update: Redwood Inference incident affecting API (started {{start_time}})\Update: {{current_state}}
Actions taken: {{actions}}
Estimated time to resolution: {{eta}}
Thanks for your patience — we’ll send another update by {{next_update_time}} or sooner if there’s a material change.

Template: Final incident summary & credit notice
Subject: Incident summary: {{incident_id}} — impact, root cause, and credits\Hello {{customer_name}},
Summary: On {{incident_date}} between {{start_time}} and {{end_time}} UTC, you may have experienced {{detailed-impact}}.
Root cause: {{root_cause_summary}}
What we fixed: {{remediation_summary}}
Customer impact: {{affected_customers_or_tenants}}
Credit: We have proposed a {{credit_amount}} credit for {{billing_period}}. If you are an enterprise customer we will apply the credit automatically; hosted customers will see the credit applied to the billing period following approval.
Next steps: The incident has been documented in a postmortem (internal link: {{postmortem_link}}). Action items are assigned and scheduled for completion.
If you have questions or need a custom reconciliation, contact {{cs_representative}}.
Thanks,
Redwood Inference Support & Product

Postmortem template checklist (minimum required fields)\- Title (incident id & short summary)\- Severity classification (S1/S2)
- Timeline (UTC, annotated with evidence links)
- Impact assessment (customers affected, SLO deviation quant, revenue exposure estimate)
- Root cause analysis (5 whys or fishbone)
- Remediation and mitigations (short term / long term)
- Action items (owner, due date, verification criteria)
- Lessons learned and follow-up review date
- Attachments: timeline.log, traces.json, grafana-snapshots.txt, customer-notices.md

Runbook excerpt: closure commands and queries\(CLI and SQL examples are illustrative — store exact saved queries with incident artifacts)\\n# Example: extract request error rate for time window\SELECT
  time_bucket('1m', ts) AS minute,
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE status >= 500) as errors,
  count(*) as total_requests
FROM requests_events
WHERE ts BETWEEN '{{start_time}}' AND '{{end_time}}'
GROUP BY minute
ORDER BY minute;

# Export grafana panel (curl example)\curl -o grafana-panel.png "https://grafana.internal/render/d-solo/{{dashboard_uid}}/{{panel_id}}?from={{from}}&to={{to}}&width=1000&height=500"

Closure timeline (recommended targets)\- T0: Incident detected / pager fired\- T0 + 30m: Initial customer ack sent (if customer-impacting)\- T0 + 60m: Stabilization or mitigation complete or next milestone update\- T0 + 4h: SRE preliminary impact calculation and credit proposal drafted\- T0 + 24h: Final incident summary published to customers; postmortem draft created\- T0 + 72h: Action items assigned and 1st remediation sprint scheduled

Game day and rotation integration
- Every game day should include a mock closure exercise: ICS confirms evidence capture, CS sends a mock final summary, and Finance practices issuing a mock credit.
- Rotation leads must ensure the on-call shadow runs through the full closure checklist once per rotation.

Escalation and legal considerations
- If an incident potentially affects regulated data or triggers contractual obligations, pause customer-facing copy and engage Legal immediately.
- For incidents involving data residency breaches, follow the security incident process in security-and-compliance/incident-response-security.

Appendices
A. Evidence archive conventions
- Incident artifacts must be stored under: gs://redwood-incident-evidence/{{year}}/{{incident_id}}/ with the following subfolders: timeline/, traces/, grafana/, customer-comm/.

B. Quick credit approval checklist (CS + Finance)\- Proposed credit amount and rationale\- Affected tenant list (CSV)\- Billing period and invoice references\- Finance approval email + ticket id
